To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Methylglyoxl, an advanced glycation end-product, accumulates in arterial wall and causes vascular contractile and relaxation dysfunction in spontaneously hypertenstive rats.
MGO accumulation causes vascular dysfunction in mesenteric arteries from SHR, which is normalized by an MGO scavenging agent, aminoguenidine.

methylglyoxal accumulation may be involved in the pathogenesis of hypertension in spontaneously hypertensive rat, at least in part through the impairment of acetylcholine-mediated relaxation and the increase in angiotensin II-mediated contraction in mesenteric arteries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of methylglyoxal accumulation and vascular contractile dysfunction.
the role of MGO in the development of hypertension in spontaneously hypertensive rat.
a new hypothesis that MGO accumulation contributes to the development of vascular contractile dysfunction and hypertension in SHR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MGO accumulation is a causative factor of vascular dysfunction in SHR.
MGO accumulation may mediate development and progression of hypertension in SHR.

AG treatment in SHR ameliorates hypertension, and this may be mediated at least in part by ameliorating impaired ACh-induced relaxation and increased Ang II-induced vasoconstriction in SHR mesenteri artery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MGO accumulation is a novel pathogenic factor for vascular dysfunction in SHR.
MGO accumulation may contribute to vascular dysfunction in SHR via increased ROS production and increased AT2R expression.

MGO accumulation may contribute to development of hypertension in SHRs by impairing endothelium-dependent vasodilation and by increasing Ang II-induced vasoconstriction via ROS production and AT2R activation, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MGO may contribute to vascular dysfunction and hypertension in SHR.
methylglyoxal accumulation is associated with vascular dysfunction in hypertension and that this effect is mediated via reactive oxygen species and angiotensin II type 2 receptors.
MGO is a novel therapeutic target for hypertension.
